headline: Siemens has invested more than $100 million in Skeleton Technologies, an Estonian energy storage firm, which pushes its value above $1 billion.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a clear AI infrastructure deal, but the valuation and the 40% benefit come from the company.
importance_line: Data center operators may get steadier power, but the claim of up to 40% more computing comes from Skeleton's own chief executive.
source: Bloomberg, as relayed by The Next Web
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Next Web, that Siemens has invested more than $100 million in Skeleton Technologies, an Estonian maker of energy storage for data centers, giving it a value of over $1 billion, with Siemens gaining exclusive rights to sell Skeleton's systems to data centers. Skeleton's chief executive, Taavi Madiberk, says good power management can allow up to 40% more computing on the chips, a claim that has not been independently checked.
notes: Original Bloomberg page blocked; text read at The Next Web, which cites Bloomberg.
